title: Link
description:
A connection between two ports: RFC 8345's link, carrying Redfish Cable's physical attributes.

Two things here are load-bearing.

First, `key` is content-addressable -- derived from the two endpoints rather than minted -- following UFM's convention. An expected link read from a cabling file and an observed link discovered on the fabric compute the SAME key, so the diff between plan and reality is a set operation instead of a matching heuristic. That diff is the validation product.

Second, `supporting_link_id` layers a link over the one carrying it, again from RFC 8345. An NVLink between two GPUs is supported by a physical cable cartridge; they are different links with different endpoints, and collapsing them loses the ability to say 'these six NVLink failures are one bad cartridge'. Diagnosing that distinction by hand is the kind of afternoon this field exists to prevent.

key.description: Content-addressable identity: `<resource>_<port>:<resource>_<port>`, with the two endpoint terms sorted lexically so the key does not depend on which end was read first. Generated by `backend/contracts/identity.py`, never hand-written -- a hand-written key that disagrees with its endpoints silently breaks the plan-versus-reality diff.

link_class.description: Must match the class of both endpoint ports. The schema cannot enforce that across records; `backend/contracts/validate.py` does.

supporting_link_id.description: The lower-layer link carrying this one, per RFC 8345 supporting-link. An NVLink points at the cartridge link beneath it.

cable.description: Redfish Cable attributes for the physical thing between the two ports. Absent for a logical link, which is how you tell the two apart.

cable_type.description: DAC, AOC, MPO trunk, NVLink cartridge, busbar tap, coolant hose.

resource_id.description: The cable's own Resource record, where it is tracked as an asset -- an NVLink cable cartridge is a serialized, replaceable, individually failing part, so it earns one. A patch cord generally does not.

speed_gbps.description: Negotiated speed on an observed link, design speed on an expected one.

observation.description: The whole point of this entity. `expected` comes from the P2P cabling file; `observed` comes from ibnetdiscover, UFM or LLDP. Missing-in-observed is an uncabled or dead link; missing-in-expected is a miscable; present in both with different speeds is a marginal link.

operational_state.description: Only meaningful on an observed link. Present because a link that exists but is down is a different defect from a link that is absent, and both are found during the same sweep.
